memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the eighth day Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel." - Lev 9:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Seven days of ordination are complete. Now comes the eighth day — the first day of actual ministry.

There is something significant about eighth days in Scripture. Seven marks completion; eight marks a fresh beginning on the other side of it. Circumcision happened on the eighth day. And Jesus rose on the first day of a new week, the day after the Sabbath — a new creation beginning where the old one had finished.

For Aaron and his sons, the preparation was over. The waiting was done. Today they would actually serve.

Every calling has an eighth day. There comes a point when the training ends and the work begins, when the praying about it gives way to doing it. That transition can be frightening. Preparation is safe; ministry is exposed.

But notice who summons them. Moses calls them out. They do not decide for themselves that they are ready — God's word through Moses tells them the day has come.

If God has been preparing you for something, He will also tell you when to begin. You do not have to manufacture your own eighth day.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I in a season of preparation or of doing — and which am I resisting?
2. Is there something God has clearly told me to begin that I keep postponing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You set both the season of preparation and the day of beginning. Give me courage to start when You say start. Amen.
